sentences.text: The animal featured a prominent crest that was triangular in shape and stood about 9.2 centimeters tall.
Its skull contained a large nasoantorbital fenestra, an opening that measured roughly forty percent of the total skull length.
Fossil evidence suggests the creature had a wingspan of nearly six meters and possessed thirty-five pairs of teeth in its upper jaw.
Researchers found the type specimen, which included a skull, atlas, and axis, in 2010 within the Romualdo Formation of the Araripe Basin in Brazil.
Renan Bantim and colleagues formally described the genus in 2014.
The generic name pays tribute to Maara, a river monster from Cariri legends known for devouring fishermen.
The suffix 'dactylus' comes from the Greek word for 'finger' and refers to the long fourth wing finger.
The specific name honors Alexander Kellner, a leading expert on Brazilian pterosaurs.
In 2019, Megan L. Jacobs and colleagues moved the species formerly known as Coloborhynchus spielbergi into this genus.
Maaradactylus belongs to the family Anhangueridae.
A 2019 phylogenetic analysis originally identified it as the closest relative of Anhanguera.
Later studies determined that Cearadactylus is a synonym of Brasileodactylus, making Brasileodactylus the true closest relative.
This pterosaur lived during the Aptian to Albian stages of the Lower Cretaceous period in northeastern Brazil.
Its existence spans the time between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
